title: The Damon Runyon Theatre
paragraphs: Radio adaptations of Damon Runyon's Broadway stories, narrated by the character 'Broadway' and populated by gamblers, gangsters, show people, dreamers, and other colorful figures of Runyon's New York.

Syndicated anthology dramatizing 52 Damon Runyon short stories. Story numbers 1-52 are stable, while two documented market/distribution schedules place the same numbered programs about thirteen weeks apart.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Earlier syndication schedule (October 3, 1948 to September 25, 1949) and Later syndication schedule (January 2, 1949 to December 25, 1949).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Damon Runyon (author), [[person|john-brown|John Brown]] (performer), Richard Sanville (director), Russell Hughes (radio adaptor and writer), Vern Carstensen (production supervisor and performer), Frank Gallop (announcer), and [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.c76079baded29531|Mayfair]].

The stories often return to Broadway and New York nightlife, show business and performers, romance and courtship, loyalty, friendship and obligation, gangsters and criminal underworld, and horse racing and racetrack culture.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar transcription syndication, Posthumous adaptation of Damon Runyon stories, Runyonesque Broadway vernacular on radio, and Independent Hollywood-star production.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|box-13|Box 13]], and [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]].
